podcast.body: This acclaimed album by Sting featured the "funky ditty" "We'll Be Together," which was a re-recorded version of a jingle he had originally penned for a Japanese Kirin Beer commercial. The album track went on to become a pop hit. "When sting re-recorded that jingle, we'll be together for his acclaimed album Nothing Like The Sun, the funky diddy became a hit, peaking on the Hot 100 at number 7 in December of 87."

podcast.body: Released in the fall of 1987, this album was named after the opening line of a Shakespeare sonnet. It was designed to fit the length of a single CD (an hour-long), while also being released as a double vinyl album, targeting the upscale 80s-yuppie compact disc market. Digitally recorded and sonically pristine, it was positioned to define Sting as "pop's Prince of Sophistication, a world-beat icon and rocks social conscience." The album was rated one of the 100 best albums of the 1980s by Rolling Stone, despite some critical dissent. "Musically, nothing like the sun positioned Sting as pop's Prince of Sophistication, a world-beat icon and rocks social conscience."
